welcome.title: Welcome to Guardian
welcome.description:
**Guardian** is a free antivirus and system-care app for Windows 10 and 11, made by one developer and built in the open.

It watches new files, startup entries, USB drives and (as administrator) every program the moment it starts. It checks them with its own engine, tells you *why* it flagged something, and never removes anything you can't undo.

fields.name: Good to know
fields.value: Guardian works with or without Windows Defender. It runs in user mode, not as a kernel driver, and it isn't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn you the first time: choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.

rules.title: Server rules
rules.description:
**1. Be decent.** No harassment, hate or personal attacks. Disagree with ideas, not people.

**2. Use the right channel.** Support goes in <#{help}>, bugs in <#{bugs}>, ideas in <#{features}>.

**3. No malware, cracks, keygens or cheats.** Not as files, not as links. Talk about samples with hashes and names only.

**4. Defensive security only.** Discuss how to detect and stop threats, not how to attack other people.

**5. No piracy.** No requests, no help, no links.

**6. Protect your privacy.** Never post passwords, tokens, API keys (including your VirusTotal key) or personal files. Never upload documents, photos or ID scans when reporting a false positive.

**7. No spam and no self-promotion** without asking staff first. No unsolicited invites or DMs.

**8. Keep it in English** in the main channels so everyone can follow.

**9. Follow the [Discord Terms](https://discord.com/terms) and [Guidelines](https://discord.com/guidelines).**

**10. Staff have the final say.** If you think a decision was wrong, ask a moderator politely in private.

fields.name: Scam warning
fields.value: Guardian staff will **never** DM you first, ask for a password, or ask you to download something outside the official [GitHub releases]({download}). If someone does, report them in <#{help}> or to a moderator.

fields.name: Is Guardian free?
fields.value: Yes. No ads, no account, no watermark.

fields.name: Do I need Windows Defender?
fields.value: No. Real-time protection, the quick, folder and deep scans, the hash lists and the signature rules all work without it. If Defender is on, the two work side by side.

fields.name: Is it a kernel-level antivirus?
fields.value: No. Guardian has no kernel driver. With administrator rights it listens to Windows' own kernel process events, so it sees every program within moments of it starting and can pause a risky one, but it can't stop a program before its first instruction. That needs a Microsoft-signed driver and a paid certificate.

fields.name: Windows says 'Windows protected your PC'
fields.value: Guardian isn't code-signed yet. Choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. Every release shows a SHA-256 checksum on GitHub, and Guardian checks it before it updates itself.

fields.name: Does it upload my files?
fields.value: Never. The optional VirusTotal check sends only a file's SHA-256 fingerprint, and only if you turn it on and add your own key.

fields.name: Can it delete a good file by mistake?
fields.value: It never deletes. Quarantine moves a file aside and you can restore it from Virus scan → Quarantine. 'It's fine' stops a file being raised again.

fields.name: Programs as they start says 'not running'
fields.value: That shield needs administrator rights. Use **Restart as administrator** in the banner at the top of Guardian.

fields.name: Where are its files?
fields.value: Settings, history and quarantine live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Guardian`. If something breaks, the end of `errors.log` in that folder is what we need.

fields.name: How do updates work?
fields.value: Guardian checks GitHub releases, verifies the installer's checksum, installs silently and reopens. You can turn the check off in Settings.

roadmap.title: What Guardian does today
roadmap.description: A short history of what has shipped.

fields.name: Scanning
fields.value: Guardian's own deep scan with signatures, behaviour checks, 9,000+ known-bad hashes and 5,000+ YARA rules. Quick scans and folder scans. Windows Defender and VirusTotal scans as extras.

fields.name: Real-time protection
fields.value: Watches new files, startup entries, USB drives and programs as they start. Optional auto-quarantine and an optional pause for high-risk programs.

fields.name: PC care
fields.value: Registry repair, disk cleanup, debloat, tracks eraser, shortcut fixer, startup and process managers, driver manager and backups, manufacturer driver checks, performance tweaks and a BIOS update assistant that never flashes firmware.

fields.name: Updates
fields.value: Self-updating installer with checksum verification.

roadmap.title: Ideas on the table
roadmap.description: These are ideas people ask for. They are **not promises** and have no dates.

fields.name: A code-signed installer
fields.value: Would remove the SmartScreen warning. Needs a paid certificate.

fields.name: A real kernel driver
fields.value: Would let Guardian block programs before they start. Needs a Microsoft-signed driver, which needs a paid certificate.

fields.name: A Linux version
fields.value: Asked for often. The app would need a new interface and a lot of the Windows-only parts rewritten.

fields.name: Your idea
fields.value: Post it in <#{features}>.

howitworks.title: How Guardian works
howitworks.description: Four steps, every time something new shows up on your PC.

fields.name: 1. Catch
fields.value: Watchers see new files in Downloads, the desktop, temp and startup folders, new startup entries, USB drives and, as administrator, every program the moment it starts (through Windows' own kernel process events).

fields.name: 2. Inspect
fields.value: The engine checks the digital signature, where the file lives and how it behaves, then 9,000+ known-bad fingerprints and 5,000+ YARA rules. All of it runs on your PC. A rule match counts as evidence weighed against the rule's confidence and the file's signature, never as a verdict by itself.

fields.name: 3. Decide
fields.value: Anything medium-risk or worse becomes an alert with the reasons in plain words. Optionally Guardian quarantines serious threats or pauses a high-risk program until you decide.

fields.name: 4. Undo
fields.value: Quarantine moves a file aside and never deletes it. Restore it any time. Every alert stays in your history.

howitworks.footer: Guardian never opens your documents, photos or ID scans, and never uploads your files.
